benchmark.title: Benchmark - jasy
benchmark.description: jasy against react-pdf, pdfmake and jsPDF on six documents - same text, same pages, same ink. The harness, the cases and the raw numbers are all here; four lines and you have your own.
benchmark.ogTitle: How fast is jasy? Here is everything we measured.
benchmark.ogDescription: Six documents against react-pdf, pdfmake and jsPDF. Same words, same pages, same ink - checked before a single number is printed. The harness and every case are in the repo.
benchmark.h1: How fast is jasy? Here is everything we measured.
benchmark.lead: Six documents, four engines, every comparison held to the same text on the same pages. jasy is a PDF engine in {pure} - no headless browser, no WASM, no JVM - and it is what {vue}, {react} and {nuxt} render with.
benchmark.meansNote: Both figures are geometric means, which is the correct average of ratios. {notIn} - it draws where these lay out, and an average across the two would mean nothing. Its comparison has its own section below, losses included.
benchmark.casesLead: Bars are to scale within a case, against its slowest engine. Every pairing was checked for the same words on the same pages before a ratio was printed.
benchmark.produced: What this run produced. Same document, same {n} page - look rather than take our word for it. | What this run produced. Same document, same {n} pages - look rather than take our word for it.
benchmark.sharedSetup: The shared setup, then the {engine} document - the file the runner imports.
benchmark.behindP1: It draws where the others lay out, and drawing is cheaper. There is no defect on either side - you are the one doing the layout. In the report case that is 73 lines of {engine} against 41 of jasy: every y coordinate, every page break, and the header redrawn after each new page. Both are on this page; read them rather than take the count.
benchmark.behindP2: That is the whole trade. You pay roughly forty milliseconds on thirteen pages, and stop writing that loop. Two of the six documents it cannot produce at all - the SVG case needs a second library, and it never kerns, so the same words do not land in the same places.
benchmark.honestH2: A benchmark written by the author of one of the engines is worth nothing until it shows what it did to catch itself.
benchmark.honestLead: So here is every rule this harness enforces - including the two that cost us the numbers we would rather be printing. They stay in.
benchmark.rule1Title: Every engine draws the same document
benchmark.rule1Body: Same words, same count, same pages - checked before a ratio is printed, and the runner refuses to print one otherwise. It has earned its keep twice, both times on our own mistakes: a case that handed react-pdf a cell too short for its line, so it drew no labels at all while the page count still matched; and a header spacing we had set on one side only, which put a whole body 8pt lower.
benchmark.rule2Body: A benchmark that repeats one string measures caching, not layout. Ours did, and the repetition helped react-pdf far more than us - on the same machine and the same day, the flowing-text case came out 45% in its favor with one repeated paragraph and 6% with 180 different ones. Real documents have no identical paragraphs, so neither do these.
benchmark.rule3Title: The settings are converted, not assumed
benchmark.rule3Body: The same word means different things in each of them: a line height multiplies the font size in jasy, the font's own natural height in pdfmake, and is not inherited into nested text at all in react-pdf. None of that is a fault - it just has to be converted, or the documents break in different places. Every conversion is pinned in the case with the reason beside it.
benchmark.rule4Title: We switch our own features off
benchmark.rule4Body: jasy keeps two lines of a paragraph together at a page break; jsPDF has no such rule. So it is turned off in the report case, on our side and react-pdf's. Handicapping ourselves is what makes it the same document.
benchmark.runLead: The harness, the six documents and the raw JSON behind this page are in the repository. It pins the versions it compares against, and prints the machine it ran on.
benchmark.runPr: Your document is not among the six? That is the fair objection to any benchmark, and the answer is a pull request - a case is one file with one function per engine.
benchmark.outro: One machine, one day, six documents. Your numbers will differ - which is the point of publishing the harness rather than only the result.
benchmark.jasyNote: Works the document out itself - line breaks, pagination, kerning, SVG. No headless browser, no WASM, no JVM.
benchmark.reactPdfNote: The same job through Yoga and a React tree. The closest comparison on this page.
benchmark.pdfmakeNote: Works it out too, with its own column and table model. Kerns, and takes SVG markup directly.
benchmark.jsPdfNote: You work out every coordinate and every page break. That is why it is quick here, and why two cases are blank.

erechnung.title: Germany's e-invoicing mandate 2025, 2027, 2028: create and validate XRechnung and ZUGFeRD
erechnung.description: Since 2025, businesses in Germany must be able to receive e-invoices, and from 2027 and 2028 they must issue them too. What applies, which formats count, which exceptions exist - and how to create and validate XRechnung and ZUGFeRD in TypeScript.
erechnung.h1: Germany's e-invoicing mandate: what applies from 2025, 2027 and 2028
erechnung.lead: Invoices between businesses in Germany are going electronic - not as a PDF attachment, but as structured data under the European standard EN 16931. This page covers what the law requires, from when, for whom - and how to create and validate conformant XRechnung and ZUGFeRD invoices yourself.
erechnung.asOf: As of November 6, 2026 · sources at the end of the page
erechnung.whatText: An e-invoice is an invoice in a structured electronic format that allows electronic processing. The format must comply with the European standard EN 16931 - or be an agreed format from which all details can be transferred correctly and completely into such a format. A PDF, a scan or a Word document is not an e-invoice but an “other invoice” (sonstige Rechnung).
erechnung.exempt1: Small-amount invoices up to 250 euros - they may always be sent as an other invoice.
erechnung.exempt2: Travel tickets, such as train and bus tickets.
erechnung.exempt3: Tax-exempt supplies under Section 4 No. 8 to 29 UStG, for example many financial and medical professions.
erechnung.exempt4: Invoices to private individuals - the mandate applies between businesses in Germany.
erechnung.createH2: Create e-invoices in TypeScript and Node.js
erechnung.createText: With {pkg} you describe the invoice once, as an object. Both halves come from it: the readable PDF/A-3 and the EN 16931 data. Totals, tax amounts and the breakdown by tax rate are calculated, not typed. No Java, no external service - your data never leaves your server.
erechnung.createPasses: This exact invoice passes the KoSIT EN 16931 business rules and the veraPDF PDF/A-3 check. For a public authority, write {call} - if a mandatory field such as the Leitweg-ID is missing, the library tells you which one before anything is sent.
erechnung.checkH2: Validate e-invoices - including those from other software
erechnung.checkText: An e-invoice is only valid once it passes the official rules: the KoSIT EN 16931 business rules for the data, and veraPDF, the reference validator for PDF/A, for the file. Our free validator runs exactly these checks - for every XRechnung and every ZUGFeRD invoice, whatever software made it. The file is checked and deleted right away, nothing is stored. If you would rather upload nothing at all, validate fully offline with the command line: {cmd}.
erechnung.disclaimer: This page explains the legal situation; it is not tax advice.

timeline.receiveText: An e-invoice no longer needs the recipient's consent. Anyone who receives invoices from businesses must be able to accept and process them.
timeline.allText: Every business may still send paper or - with the recipient's consent - another electronic format such as a plain PDF.
timeline.smallText: Only for businesses with a total turnover of at most 800,000 euros in the previous year. Invoices via EDI are also allowed until the end of 2027, with the recipient's consent.
timeline.issueText: Between businesses in Germany, every invoice is an e-invoice - apart from exceptions such as small-amount invoices.

formats.xrechnungWhat: Pure XML (CII or UBL syntax), the German flavor of EN 16931.
formats.xrechnungWhen: Mandatory for public authorities (B2G), usable anywhere in B2B.
formats.zugferdWhat: A readable PDF/A-3 with the EN 16931 XML embedded - people and machines read the same file.
formats.zugferdWhen: The standard in B2B: the customer sees a PDF, their accounting reads the data.

faq.pdfQ: Is a PDF sent by email an e-invoice?
faq.pdfA: No. An e-invoice is an invoice in a structured electronic format that allows electronic processing (Section 14(1) UStG). A plain PDF is an “other invoice” and only allowed during the transition periods. A ZUGFeRD PDF, by contrast, carries the structured XML inside it.
faq.issueQ: From when do I have to issue e-invoices?
faq.issueA: From January 1, 2027. Businesses with a total turnover of at most 800,000 euros in the previous year may send other invoices until the end of 2027; from January 1, 2028 the mandate applies to all businesses in Germany (Section 27(38) UStG).
faq.receiveQ: Do I already have to be able to receive e-invoices?
faq.receiveA: Yes, since January 1, 2025. The transition rules cover issuing only, not receiving.
faq.formatQ: XRechnung or ZUGFeRD - which do I need?
faq.formatA: Both comply with the European standard EN 16931. XRechnung is required for public authorities. In B2B, ZUGFeRD is common because the file is a readable PDF at the same time.
faq.exemptA: Small-amount invoices up to 250 euros (Section 33 UStDV) and travel tickets (Section 34 UStDV) may always be sent as other invoices. Tax-exempt supplies under Section 4 No. 8 to 29 UStG and invoices to private individuals are not covered by the mandate.
faq.validQ: How do I check whether an e-invoice is valid?
faq.validA: With the official rules: the KoSIT EN 16931 business rules for the data, and veraPDF, the reference validator for PDF/A, for the file. Our free validator runs exactly these checks, for invoices from any software.
